 Alexandra Eala
 Alexandra Eala has given Philippine tennis a place on some of the sport’s biggest stages. From childhood practice sessions with her grandfather to championship matches against leading professionals, her progress reflects years of training, family support and personal sacrifice.
 Her success reaches beyond trophies. She represents a country with a deep love of sport but a smaller presence in elite tennis. Each milestone has strengthened her connection with Filipino supporters worldwide.
 At 21, Eala combines a growing tennis career with major brand partnerships. Yet her story began with a simple wish to spend time with family on court.
 Alexandra Eala Quick Bio
 Detail Facts

 Alexandra Eala’s Early Life and Family
 Born in Quezon City, Eala grew up in a household where sport and education mattered. Her parents supported her ambitions while helping her develop discipline beyond tennis.
 Her mother, Rizza, competed for the Philippines in swimming. She earned a bronze medal in the 100 metre backstroke at the 1985 Southeast Asian Games. She later built a corporate career and served as Globe Telecom’s chief financial officer.
 Her father, Mike, is a business executive. Both parents played important roles in managing the demands of travel, schooling and competition.
 The Grandfather Who Started Her Tennis Journey
 Eala began playing at four. Her grandfather, Roberto “Bobby” Maniego, introduced her to tennis and became her first mentor.
 He was a club player who enjoyed teaching family members. For young Alex, practice offered time with him and her older brother, Miko.
 Those sessions gradually became more serious. Tennis taught her patience, effort and how to respond when a point went wrong.
 Miko also pursued the sport and later played university tennis at Pennsylvania State University.
 Alexandra Eala’s Education and Move to Spain
 Eala attended Immaculate Conception Academy and Colegio San Agustin before continuing her education in Spain.
 At 13, she moved to the Rafa Nadal Academy in Mallorca. Leaving home meant adjusting to a different country, demanding training and greater independence.
 Her brother joined her, giving her familiar support during that change. Their parents remained involved despite the distance.
 Balancing School and Competitive Tennis
 Eala graduated from the academy’s school programme in June 2023. Rafael Nadal attended the ceremony, while Iga Świątek took part as a guest speaker.
 Her graduation marked an academic achievement alongside her sporting progress. There is no confirmed university degree.
 Living in Spain helped her learn Spanish. She also speaks English and Filipino. Her multilingual background is clear, although assigning her one fixed accent would oversimplify how she communicates.
 Alexandra Eala’s Career: From Junior Titles to Senior Success
 Her development followed a steady path through junior events and professional tournaments. Success did not arrive through one match. It grew from years of competing against stronger opponents.
 Junior Championships That Built Her Reputation
 In 2018, Eala won Les Petits As in France, a major international event for players aged 14 and under. She defeated Linda Nosková in the final.
 More success followed at junior Grand Slams. She won the 2020 Australian Open girls’ doubles title with Priska Madelyn Nugroho, then the 2021 French Open girls’ doubles championship with Oksana Selekhmeteva.
 Alexandra Eala’s Historic US Open Victory
 Her biggest junior singles achievement came in 2022. She defeated Lucie Havlíčková 6–2, 6–4 in the US Open girls’ final.
 The victory made her the first Filipina to win a junior Grand Slam singles championship.
 That distinction matters: junior championships and senior Grand Slam titles belong to different levels of competition.
 Building Experience on the ITF Circuit
 Eala began her professional career in 2020. In January 2021, aged 15, she won her first professional singles title at W15 Manacor.
 She added Chiang Rai in 2022, followed by Yecla and Roehampton in 2023. Her 2024 victory at W100 Vitoria Gasteiz became her fifth ITF singles title.
 She also earned doubles titles, developing teamwork and skills that complemented her singles game.
 These smaller tournaments gave her experience with travel, recovery and the pressure of earning ranking points.
 The Breakthrough Season of 2025
 Miami changed the scale of her career. Eala reached the semifinals after victories that included Madison Keys and Iga Świątek.
 Her performance helped her enter the WTA Top 100 and brought wider attention to Philippine tennis.
 She then reached her first WTA Tour final at Eastbourne. Later, she won the Guadalajara WTA 125 championship.
 A WTA 125 title is distinct from a regular WTA Tour title, an important difference when describing her achievements.
 New Heights in 2026
 Eala won the Birmingham WTA 125 title and reached Wimbledon’s fourth round in 2026. Her Wimbledon campaign included another victory over Świątek.
 Washington delivered her first WTA Tour singles championship. She defeated Jessica Pegula 4–6, 6–4, 6–0 in the final.
 That result made her the first player representing the Philippines to win a WTA Tour singles title.
 She reached world No. 18 and advanced to the third round of the US Open.
 Alexandra Eala’s Playing Style and Coaching
 Eala plays left handed with a two handed backhand. Her game combines movement, controlled groundstrokes and a willingness to keep fighting through long rallies.
 She can absorb pace and turn defence into attack. Her return game also helps her challenge opponents who rely on strong serves.
 Joan Bosch and Sandro Viaene have contributed to her development through the academy’s coaching structure.
 Nadal’s academy has been central to her training, but Nadal should not be described as her regular personal coach.
 Alexandra Eala’s Medals for the Philippines
 National competition remains an important part of her career.
 At the 2021 Southeast Asian Games, held in 2022, she earned bronze medals in women’s singles, women’s team tennis and mixed doubles.
 She added women’s singles and mixed doubles bronze medals at the 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023.
 At the 2025 SEA Games, she won singles gold and two further bronzes. Her singles victory ended a 26 year Philippine wait for gold in that event.
 She also earned singles bronze at the 2026 Asian Games.
 Alexandra Eala’s Net Worth, Earnings and Income
 Eala’s exact net worth is not verified. Prize money measures tournament earnings, while net worth depends on assets, debts, expenses and retained income.
 The Australian Open’s official statistics showed career earnings of US$3,395,880 on 28 October 2026.
 That figure does not represent the amount she has available to spend. Professional tennis involves coaching fees, travel, accommodation, equipment costs and taxes.
 Does She Receive a Salary?
 Eala does not have a publicly established fixed salary comparable to a salaried employee.
 Her income comes mainly from tournament prize money and commercial partnerships.
 Forbes estimated that her earnings outside tennis competitions exceeded US$5 million during the 12 months before its August 2026 feature.
 This estimate covers a different period from annual tournament earnings. The figures should not be combined into a precise yearly income.
 Sponsorships, Companies and Business Ventures
 Her commercial partners include Nike, Babolat, Globe Telecom, BPI, Locally and Milo Philippines.
 Additional partnerships involve Marriott Bonvoy, Panasonic Philippines and Philippine Airlines.
 These agreements connect her with sportswear, equipment, banking, travel and consumer brands.
 However, being a brand ambassador does not mean she owns those companies. No verified evidence establishes a separate company, investment fund or independent business founded by her.
 Alexandra Eala’s Relationships, Religion and Personal Life
 Eala keeps much of her private life separate from professional tennis. No confirmed marriage or children have been announced.
 In March 2025, she directly denied that tennis player Coleman Wong was her boyfriend. She described them as friends.
 That answer addressed a specific rumour at that time. It does not establish her current dating status.
 Faith and Interests Beyond Tennis
 Eala has spoken about reciting the Hail Mary and Our Father during matches when she was younger. Coverage of her upbringing also identifies Catholic influences.
 Her comments support discussing those prayer habits without making claims about her present religious observance.
 Away from competition, she enjoys Spanish music, comedy and horror films. Ice cream, rice and milk tea are among her favourite foods and drinks.
 Alexandra Eala’s Latest News and Developing Legacy
 On 28 October 2026, Eala defeated Talia Gibson 4–6, 6–2, 6–0 to reach the Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals in Tokyo.
 The comeback set up another meeting with Diana Shnaider, who had beaten her at Ningbo the previous week.
 Her growing influence also earned recognition through TIME100 Next 2026, with Rafael Nadal writing the accompanying tribute.
 Eala’s legacy remains unfinished. She has already expanded the possibilities for Philippine tennis through junior championships, national medals and senior victories.
 Her next challenge is sustaining that progress across full seasons. The ambition is clear: compete for major titles while continuing to improve. Her achievements now give young Filipino players a stronger reason to believe that the same courts are within their reach.
 FAQs
 Who is Alexandra Eala?
 Alexandra Eala is a Filipino professional tennis player. She won the 2022 US Open girls’ singles title and trains at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Spain.
 How old is Alexandra Eala?
 Alexandra Eala is 21 years old as of October 2026. She was born on 23 May 2005 in Quezon City, Philippines.
 Who are Alexandra Eala’s parents?
 Her parents are Michael “Mike” Eala, a business executive, and Rosemarie “Rizza” Maniego Eala, a former national swimmer and corporate executive.
 Is Alexandra Eala married?
 Alexandra Eala has not publicly confirmed a marriage. She keeps her romantic life private.
 Does Alexandra Eala have siblings?
 Yes, she has an older brother, Michael Francis “Miko” Eala, who played university tennis at Pennsylvania State University.
